newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks suspended term against Zaire ex-envoy.
newsitem.headline: France seeks suspended term against Zaire ex-envoy.

text.p: A state prosecutor asked for a three-year suspended prison sentence on Tuesday for Zaire's former ambassador to Paris for the manslaughter of two boys in a traffic accident on the French Riviera.

Ex-envoy Ramazani Baya faced the court in the Riviera capital Nice in a rare case of a diplomat being brought to justice in the country he officially served in. The court will announce its verdict on April 29.

Baya returned to France in January without his diplomatic immunity. Zaire said he had been relieved of his ambassadorial duties, but Baya said he had resigned so he could face a French court and clear his conscience.

He was on his way to visit Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, recuperating from cancer therapy at his villa, when he hit Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing in the nearby resort of Menton on November 23.
Police have said he was driving at more than twice the legal speed limit.
Prosecutor Didier Durand said he understood the parents of the boys would be disappointed that he was seeking a moderate sentence.
"We need to be reasonable although we feel inclined to pass judgement with our heart...Justice cannot return your children to you. You will be disappointed," he told them.
He asked for a three-year suspended sentence and a 20,000-franc ($3,500) fine with 4,000 francs ($700) in damages and a three-year ban on driving in France.
The charges of manslaughter aggravated by unsafe and careless driving carry a penalty of up to five years in prison and a 500,000 franc ($88,000) fine.
"This is a disaster, I no longer have any faith in justice. I had expected a more severe request (from the prosecutor)," Raphael's father Patrick Lenoir told reporters.
"I had promised to come back to France and face French justice. I kept my promises to the full," Baya told reporters.
Lawyers bickered over how free his decision was.
"(Baya) created a precedent in the diplomatic world by accepting to come to trial," his lawyer Francis Szpiner said.
The lawyer for the boys' parents, Gilbert Collard, said Baya had bowed to political pressure and Mobutu had lifted his diplomatic immunity to please Paris while he was staying in France.

Relatives and neighbours of the two boys had demonstrated to demand that Baya be brought to justice, and the French government had asked Zaire to lift his immunity so he could face trial. ($ = 5.70 French Francs)
